query_snapshot: What corrosion mechanism does NBS Circular 592 associate with hydrochloric acid and other halide-containing solutions attacking stainless steel?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- NBS Circular 592 states that hydrochloric acid and some solutions containing halide ions attack the passive film on stainless steel. [nbscircular592.pdf, p. 60, chunk 2b809bc1]
- NBS Circular 592 states that this attack produces corrosion of the pitting type on stainless steel. [nbscircular592.pdf, p. 60, chunk 2b809bc1]
- NBS Circular 592 states that additions of molybdenum reduce the susceptibility of stainless steels to pitting corrosion. [nbscircular592.pdf, p. 60, chunk 2b809bc1]
